text.arabic_uthmani: إِن كَانَتْ إِلَّا صَيْحَةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ فَإِذَا هُمْ خَٰمِدُونَ

words.gloss_range: restrictive negation that opens an only-frame rather than a condition
words.prose: {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}}) opens as negation, not condition. Its first effect is to empty the event-field before the exception names the single remaining cause, so the reader is not asked to imagine a hypothetical punishment but to watch every alternative excluded. The opening sound also binds closely to the following copular clause, making the restriction feel attached from the first word.

topics.headline: restrictive negation, not condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins by excluding every alternative cause before allowing the one shout to remain.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the particle as restrictive negation with the later exception, not conditional syntax.

topics.headline: restriction governs the ayah opening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first word makes narrowing the ayah's opening move, before the cause is named.
topics.reason: The clause is syntactically forced as a restrictive frame, so the opening particle controls the reader's approach to the whole cause clause.

topics.headline: audible bond to the copular clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the opening negation is not only semantic but audibly tied to the assertion it limits.
topics.reason: The phonetic observation is locally coherent and reinforces, rather than replaces, the grammatical restriction.

words.gloss_range: completed copular occurrence that identifies the event as the single shout
words.root_gloss_range: being, occurrence, and temporal predication; local grammar selects the past copular event-identity use, while other branches such as place, suretyship, and submission are not active here
words.prose: {{ar:كَانَتْ}} ({{tr:kānat}}) makes the punishment event a completed past fact and then lets the predicate define what that fact was: a single cry. Its feminine agreement and hidden subject pull the clause toward the shout rather than a vague event, so the instrument becomes the event's identity. A variant nominative reading can shift the mechanism toward occurrence, but the canonical accusative predicate keeps the local force as identity-through-copula. The word's broad open vowels also give the restriction a small acoustic lead-in before the line tightens into the named sound-event. The same formula returns in the resurrection scene (36:53), making this copular frame one mold that can carry opposed outcomes.

topics.headline: event identified by its predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the event is not narrated in steps; it is identified as the cry itself.
topics.reason: The standard local parse treats the verb as a copular past verb with an accusative predicate, making event identity the central grammatical payoff.

topics.headline: feminine agreement and hidden subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the hidden event is recoverable only through compact agreement with the shout phrase.
topics.reason: The verb is 3fs and the bundle marks an unexpressed feminine subject controlled by the restrictive predicate.

topics.headline: completed event before sudden result
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the cause-side is already complete before the result clause appears.
topics.reason: The perfect form supports the ayah's compression by making the event a completed past occurrence.

topics.headline: variant shifts identity toward occurrence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that accepted case variation preserves the one-shout restriction while changing whether the shout defines the event or stands as the event that occurred.
topics.reason: The variant is useful as contrast, but the local canonical output remains governed by the accusative predicate parse.

topics.headline: same mold, opposed outcomes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same one-shout formula used for extinction here returns for gathering in 36:53.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows supply concrete same-surah references, and the local formula is compatible with the marked single-shout construction.

topics.headline: agent-light pivot into aftermath
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the discourse shift from denied heavenly deployment (36:28) into a minimal, agent-light event identity.
topics.reason: The boundary and clause evidence support a compressed first beat that pivots directly into the result clause.

topics.headline: paced release toward the cry
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a small acoustic lead-in before the clause releases into the named sound-event.
topics.reason: The phonetic row adds a distinct local payoff and does not contradict the grammatical guardrails.

words.gloss_range: exception particle completing the restrictive only-frame and preserving one cause as the whole remainder
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَّا}} ({{tr:illā}}) is the boundary where negation turns into exclusivity. It keeps the shout inside the event-cause class, not as an outside afterthought, and makes that one remaining item equal to all that happened. Because it comes after denial, the cause arrives late and small: only a cry, after every larger imagined mechanism has been removed.

topics.headline: exception boundary after negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the cry is the only surviving member of the event-cause field, not an unrelated afterthought.
topics.reason: The particle is locally paired with the opening negator to form a restrictive construction.

topics.headline: exception becomes onlyness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the double force of exception and restriction: alternatives are removed and the single cry becomes sufficient.
topics.reason: The local construction licenses both the exception layer and the restrictive only-force.

topics.headline: cause arrives after denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah moves from the prior denial of deployment (36:28) to the minimal positive remainder in this clause.
topics.reason: The boundary row gives a concrete prior-ayah movement, and the local syntax supports delayed presentation of the cause.

words.gloss_range: an indefinite single cry or blast functioning as the event's predicate and destructive cause
words.root_gloss_range: loud voice, shout, cry, and terrifying punitive cry; local grammar selects the instant destructive sound-event, while unrelated branches such as plant visibility or date names are not active
words.prose: {{ar:صَيْحَةً}} ({{tr:ṣayḥatan}}) is the noun that the whole restriction leaves standing. In the canonical parse it is the accusative predicate of the copular clause, so the hidden event is identified as a cry; secondary case and cognate-accusative possibilities show how strongly the word can bear the event, but they do not replace the local predicate role. Its loud, piercing cry or blast value is operative rather than ambient: one vocal eruption stands in for every larger instrument of punishment. Its instant-noun form, indefiniteness, and adjective make the cry one bounded pulse, not diffuse noise or a repeated process, and the paired indefinite endings make that pulse feel compact in recitation. The same single-shout formula links this scene to sudden judgment and transformation within Surah 36 (36:49; 36:53) and beyond it (38:15; 54:31), while here the audible eruption is answered by extinguished silence.

topics.headline: predicate that functions as cause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the cry is not scenery; it is the predicate that names the event and the mechanism that destroys.
topics.reason: The bundle identifies the word as the accusative predicate of the copular verb, and the CRITICAL rows coherently preserve its causal force.

topics.headline: case variants expose alternate event roles
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the cry can be grammatically construed as defining, occurring, or instantiating the event, while the canonical local parse keeps it as predicate.
topics.reason: Accepted and secondary readings are useful as contrast, but the local standard evidence selects accusative predicate governance.

topics.headline: piercing destructive cry
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a concrete loud, piercing sound-event strong enough to replace any larger instrument of punishment.
topics.reason: The V4 evidence supports loud cry and punitive cry branches, and the local result selects the destructive sound-event sense.

topics.headline: one bounded pulse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that morphology and indefiniteness package the destructive sound as one minimal pulse.
topics.reason: The QAC row marks the word as an instant-event noun, and the local adjective reinforces singularity.

topics.headline: single-shout formula network
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this cry belongs to a recurring formula of sudden judgment or transformation, including 36:49, 36:53, 38:15, and 54:31.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete references and the local phrase matches the recurring single-shout formula.

topics.headline: sound answered by extinguished stillness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sensory reversal from a maximum sound-event to extinguished silence.
topics.reason: The ayah's cause-result structure directly pairs the single cry with the final extinguished predicate.

topics.headline: sharp texture and paired cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word's sound texture and paired endings make the cause feel abrupt, compact, and bounded.
topics.reason: The phonetic and cadence rows support the same local compactness already established by grammar and morphology.

words.gloss_range: feminine accusative indefinite adjective marking the cry as one, sole, and sufficient
words.root_gloss_range: oneness, singleness, isolation, peerless uniqueness, and divine oneness; local grammar selects adjective-level singleness and sufficiency attached to the cry
words.prose: {{ar:وَٰحِدَةً}} ({{tr:wāḥidatan}}) is not a detached number. It agrees fully with the cry as its adjective, so the cause becomes a single syntactic unit: one cry, sufficient by itself. Because the adjective remains indefinite with the noun, the phrase stays unnamed and minimal while still ruling out a plural or repeated shout sequence. A nominative variant can raise the phrase's case, but it does not loosen the adjective's core work: the event remains one and unsupplemented. Its position at the end of the cause-beat lets the phrase shrink once more before the result appears, and the paired endings audibly bind the cry and its oneness. The phrase returns at Surah 36's three single-shout moments (36:29; 36:49; 36:53). The root's divine-oneness branch is real elsewhere, but here the local grammar keeps that pressure narrowed to numerical and causal singleness, not a divine-title claim.

topics.headline: one attached to the cry
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that oneness is grammatically fused to the cry rather than floating as a separate count.
topics.reason: The adjective agrees with the noun in gender, case, and indefiniteness, and attachment evidence marks the adjective relation as strongly licensed.

topics.headline: singleness becomes sufficiency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that one means no repeated blow, no second cause, and no supplementary process.
topics.reason: The root evidence supports singleness and isolation, while the restrictive frame makes that singleness causally sufficient.

topics.headline: unnamed one-unit phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the phrase is minimal and unnamed while still ruling out plurality or repetition.
topics.reason: The word is a feminine indefinite adjective on the numeral pattern, directly modifying the cry.

topics.headline: variant preserves one-ness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the adjective's core singleness survives even when the variant raises the noun phrase's case.
topics.reason: The accepted variant changes case alignment with the noun, not the adjective's semantic work.

topics.headline: single-shout refrain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same one-shout phrase frames past destruction, awaited doom, and resurrection in Surah 36 (36:29; 36:49; 36:53).
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete same-surah occurrences and the local adjective participates in the recurring phrase.

topics.headline: beat-end singularity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the last cause-side word seals the beat by making the cry audibly and syntactically one.
topics.reason: The adjective's position and matching ending strengthen the already licensed noun-adjective unity.

topics.headline: divine oneness branch kept local
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the root's broader oneness field can intensify the cry's exclusivity, while local grammar keeps the word from becoming a divine-oneness title.
topics.reason: V4 includes a divine-oneness branch for the root, but this local adjective modifies the cry, so the surviving payoff is narrowed to isolated sufficiency.

words.gloss_range: bound consequence particle marking immediate cause-result sequence
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) is the smallest visible hinge between cause and result. It turns the one cry into the direct ground of the final state, with no room for an interval or an independent aftermath scene. The second clause unfolds what the restricted cause already entails: once there was only one cry, their extinguished condition is the result. As it fuses with the following surprise particle, the grammar and surface form both make the transition feel immediate.

topics.headline: direct cause-result hinge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final state is grammatically tied to the cry as its direct consequence.
topics.reason: The result clause is syntactically linked to the restrictive cause, and QAC marks immediate consequence.

topics.headline: result unfolds the cause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second clause reveals what was already entailed by the one cry.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL faṣīḥa and immediate-sequence readings are compatible with the local cause-result architecture.

topics.headline: one-letter fused transition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a one-letter connector carries the whole zero-gap transition into the sudden-result phrase.
topics.reason: The surface proclitic and its attachment to the following particle reinforce the locally licensed immediate consequence.

words.gloss_range: surprise adverb introducing an already-realized nominal result, not a conditional when-clause
words.prose: {{ar:إِذَا}} ({{tr:idhā}}) is the surprise particle here, not conditional wording. It introduces a nominal clause as a discovered state: the result is already there when the clause opens. Joined with the preceding connector, it double-codes the zero-gap movement from one cry to the revealed aftermath, and its abrupt onset suits the sharp turn into extinction.

topics.headline: surprise particle, not condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the result is suddenly discovered as fact, not suspended as a when-or-if condition.
topics.reason: QAC explicitly identifies the word as surprise idhā introducing a nominal sentence, not a conditional particle.

topics.headline: discovered completed state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the aftermath is presented as an already-standing condition rather than a narrated action.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence links the particle to the final predication, and the CRITICAL rows preserve the sudden discovered-state payoff.

topics.headline: fused zero-gap transition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that immediate sequence and sudden appearance stack into one compact transition.
topics.reason: The local construction combines the preceding consequence particle with surprise idhā, supporting the zero-gap result.

topics.headline: abrupt result onset
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that grammar, spelling, and sound together make the entry into the result clause abrupt.
topics.reason: The phonetic and surface-form observations reinforce the same locally licensed surprise transition.

words.gloss_range: detached third-person masculine plural pronoun making the previously established townspeople the visible subject of the result state
words.prose: {{ar:هُمْ}} ({{tr:hum}}) gives the destroyed collective its own visible subject slot. The pronoun is detached and definite, so the result does not introduce new victims; it points back to the established people and makes them bear the final predicate. After the story has passed through the individual man's relation to his people, this plural pronoun shifts the focus to the collective fate and opens the nominal closure unit. The closure lands as subject plus state rather than a verb of dying, with the short pronoun yielding to the longer extinguished predicate.

topics.headline: detached visible subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the destroyed group is made visible as subject before the final state is assigned.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the pronoun as the independent subject of the nominal result clause.

topics.headline: same townspeople, now collective
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shift from the individual story boundary to the whole group as result-subject.
topics.reason: The bundle resolves the pronoun to the previously established people, while the CRITICAL rows preserve the shift from singular individual focus to plural collective fate.

topics.headline: opening of the final state clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah closes with subject plus state rather than with a verb of dying.
topics.reason: The pronoun begins the final nominal predication and therefore helps make the aftermath static and complete.

topics.headline: ground-level result after divine declaration
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the discourse move from divine declaration in 36:28 to the observed collective residue in 36:29.
topics.reason: The boundary evidence supports the shift from prior divine speech to the observed state of the collective.

words.gloss_range: plural active participial predicate describing the people as extinguished, cooled, and lifeless
words.root_gloss_range: fire dying down, heat or fever subsiding, and life or consciousness falling still; local usage applies the extinguished-still image to a human collective
words.prose: {{ar:خَٰمِدُونَ}} ({{tr:khāmidūn}}) is the final predicate, so the ayah lands not on the cry but on the state left after it. The word applies the root's fire-extinction and heat-subsiding field to people: they are not merely reported dead but imagined as animation, heat, and sound gone still, like cooled residue after former motion. Its active participial, masculine plural form makes the extinguished condition a settled identity distributed across the collective, not passive victim morphology or a finite death event. The rare root links this scene with the harvested-extinguished ruin of 21:15, while 36:29 isolates the extinguishing image after the one cry and contrasts with the later gathered result after the same formula (36:53). Its back, muffled sound helps the final word enact the movement from piercing cry to smothered stillness. After the elevated denial of heavenly deployment in 36:28, the register has dropped to bare observed residue.

topics.headline: final nominal predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah closes on a settled state assigned to the people, not on a narrated act of dying.
topics.reason: The word is the nominative predicate of the final nominal clause and occupies ayah-final closure position.

topics.headline: fire, heat, and life gone still
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that death is pictured as extinguishing and cooling, not merely as generic killing.
topics.reason: V4 supports fire-extinction, heat-subsiding, and lifelessness branches, and the local human predicate selects their figurative convergence.

topics.headline: embodied plural state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the form presents the people as bearers of an achieved extinguished condition, not passive objects in a narrated process.
topics.reason: The word is an active participle in masculine plural agreement with the pronoun, functioning as predicate of the nominal clause.

topics.headline: sound answered by silence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah's movement from sonic force to cooled, silent nullity.
topics.reason: The local cause-result structure pairs the single cry with this extinguished-state predicate.

topics.headline: rare extinction field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this is a specialized Quranic extinction word, not routine death vocabulary.
topics.reason: The contextual evidence marks the root/form as low occurrence, and the rows preserve that rarity as closure pressure.

topics.headline: 21:15 and 36:53 contrasts
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 21:15 pairs extinguishing with harvested ruin, while 36:53 uses the same shout formula for gathering rather than extinction.
topics.reason: The concrete inter-ayah references are compatible with the local word and clarify the distinctive simplicity of the final image.

topics.headline: minimal cause, total result
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the structural disproportion: one sound-event at the start-side and the whole collective fixed in one final state.
topics.reason: The ayah's two clauses pair the singular cause phrase with the plural nominal result.

topics.headline: muffled final sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final word's sound surface helps enact the move from piercing cry to smothered stillness.
topics.reason: The phonetic rows add a distinct surface payoff that coheres with the final extinguished-state meaning.

topics.headline: bare annihilation report
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the drop from theological denial in 36:28 to a compressed observed residue in 36:29.
topics.reason: The boundary evidence supports a discourse shift completed by the final predicate.

baseline_models.mechanism: A single alarming sound is presented as the entire occurring input, and the fa-idha transition maps it without an intervening process onto a plural cessation of life or awareness.

context_deltas.mechanism: The narrative first expands agency from two emissaries to a reinforced third, then explicitly denies any descending supporting host immediately before the focus. Against that escalation and negation, one cry is not merely a count but an anti-logistical concentration of decisive force.

structural_cues: 36:14 explicitly moves from two to reinforcement by a third.
36:28 immediately precedes the focus and twice negates sending down while naming a host.
36:29 restricts the whole event to one cry with إِلَّا and وَاحِدَةً.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies numeric escalation, reinforcement, and the explicit absence of a descending host; I infer that their juxtaposition with one cry creates a scale contrast. A live alternative is that 36:14 and 36:28 describe unrelated phases without calibrating the force of وَاحِدَةً.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because 36:80's green-tree ignition is remote from the human group in 36:29. It remains anchored because the focus branch explicitly images flame becoming quiet, while 36:80 supplies green material, active fire, and ignition. Downstream prose should label it a material analogy, not claim that the people are literal fuel, that the two ayat form an explicit pair, or that ember residue guarantees survival.

strongest_changes: The explicit no-host prelude turns 'one' into concentrated sufficiency rather than incidental counting.
The repeated single-cry frames in 36:49 and 36:53 recast 36:29 as one output of a recurrent collective state-transition pattern.
The later blast, raising, and rapid emergence qualify the focus as a historical endpoint rather than eternal inertia.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet exposed a near-verbatim inversion: 36:29 moves by one cry to collective stillness, while 36:53 moves by one cry to total gathered presence. The surrounding no-army, resurrection, performative-speech, and fire materials made the focus read as compressed state change rather than a bare death notice.
remaining_uncertainties: The ember-residue nuance belongs to a live branch of خ م د but may be weaker here than the direct death or unconsciousness branch.
The command-like force of the cry depends on a reader-supplied link to 36:82 and should remain exploratory.
The repeated cries may share only a suddenness formula rather than one functional operator.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **A single voice extinguishes a noisy collective.** `ص ي ح` B001 is loud voice and B002 terrifying cry; `و ح د` B002 is a single unit; `خ م د` B001 is a flame falling still and B003 the stilling of life. The town's many speeches and threats collapse under one cry. I infer that concentrated command reverses dispersed hostile noise into silence. The ayah reads as acoustic and thermal extinguishing at once.
2. **Stillness reverses their claimed agency.** `ك و ن` B001 supplies occurrence, and the sudden *fa-idha* marks immediate state change. They had threatened to make pain touch the envoys (36:18); now one event makes them inert without an army. The packet gives the reversal; I infer it exposes how little causal control their threats possessed.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 36:53 repeats the one-cry construction but produces gathering rather than extinction. The later reuse corrected any assumption that the cry has one intrinsic effect; command and context determine its role.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **One alarming voice equalizes the crowd into stillness.** **ص ي ح B002** anchors the terrifying punitive cry; **و ح د B005** permits things to count as one through a shared respect; **خ م د B003** anchors the stilling of life or consciousness. The prior ayah denies a gathered army, and 36:32 later names all as gathered. The packet supplies one event, plural recipients, and a common state; the inferred arrow is *a unitary signal collapses social plurality into one shared cessation*. “One” thus describes both cause and homogenized effect.
2. **The extinguished flame remains conceptually reversible.** **خ م د B001** supplies a flame falling still while embers may remain. Within the forward window, 36:31 asks about destroyed generations, 36:32 gathers all, and 36:33 displays dead earth made alive. Those packet cues activate the material analogy; the abductive arrow is *death-like stillness can conceal capacity for reactivation, as an ember or dead ground does*. **خَٰمِدُونَ** reads as extinguished activity without proving final nonreturn.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: **Later surprise.** 36:33 makes dead earth live and bring out grain, directly strengthening the ember-like reversibility of **خَٰمِدُونَ**; 36:34's released springs further show still ground concealing active capacity.

occurrence_evidence_trim.note: TRIMMED, NOT ABSENT. dictionary_entry.occurrence_evidence.occurrences and .ayahs are removed from every root by design: they are a per-occurrence QAC concordance and character-span alignment table carrying zero readings, branches or senses, and they dominated bundle size (~1.5 MB for a single common root). occurrence_evidence.summary (corpus frequency) and .forms (inflectional inventory) are retained. Dictionary/gloss branches are kept in full for every included Furuq root target.

branch_policy.note: No branch filtering is applied. Every branch present in each included dictionary/gloss root entry is kept.

root_mapping.policy: Use the dominant Furuq root for every QAC root, and include non-dominant Furuq targets as additional root_lexicon entries when qac-furuq-v4-root-map marks the QAC root as split.
